title: "About / Contribute"
subtitle: "Purpose, editorial rules, and how to add evidence"
---

## What this site is

The CSIL History Archive is a public website for a source-based history of Choice in Supports for Independent Living (CSIL) in British Columbia. It privileges an annotated bibliography and source-location records over a closed story. Core history chapters reconstruct what public sources support; missing documents and conflicting dates stay visible.

The site is intentionally small and durable: Markdown files, structured front matter, a bibliography file, and static HTML. There is no database or application backend.

## What this site is not

- A complete history of CSIL or independent living in British Columbia (core chapters are reconstructions from cited sources; many documents remain wanted)
- A current-program handbook or benefits explainer
- An advocacy or campaign landing page
- A place to store private employer, health, or correspondence files

## How to read the history

When this archive was first planned, a possible order of events and a set of working dates were suggested so later evidence would have a place to land. The [Creekview chapter](history/creekview.qmd) reconstructs the mid-1980s project from 1984–89 sources we have read, and it also holds the earlier housing-and-support context (the [Origins](history/origins.qmd) page explains that choice). It still does not treat Creekview as a proven predecessor of ECPM or CSIL. ECPM, CSIL design/pilot, and later evolution now have cited chapters; the overall Creekview → ECPM → CSIL sequence stays a **possible reading order, not a proven official sequence**, on [History](history/index.qmd) and the [Timeline](timeline.qmd).

## Editorial principles

The full contributor guide is [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/jordanforge-ca/csil-history/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md). In short:

1. Evidence before narrative.
2. Prefer sources from the time, or close to the events.
3. Separate fact, attribution, and interpretation.
4. Preserve disagreement (including 1993 versus 1994 as a CSIL “established” year, and later official 1994-pilot / 1995-province-wide wording versus 1995 newspaper “new/pilot” language).
5. Keep advocacy out of the historical record.
6. Design for accessibility first.
7. Respect living participants; publish personal material only with permission.

A short [summary of what the evidence does and does not show](history/index.qmd#state-of-the-evidence) is on the History page.

## How to contribute {#how-to-contribute}

Useful contributions include:

- a catalogue record for a public document, with a stable link
- a correction to a citation, date precision, or status label
- a scan or transcript **only** when redistribution is clearly permitted
- an oral-history note that already has publication permission

How to do it:

1. Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/jordanforge-ca/csil-history/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
2. Copy the [example source record](sources/example-template-source-record.qmd).
3. Use the [source metadata schema](docs/source-metadata.qmd) and [controlled vocabularies](docs/vocabularies.qmd).
4. Open a pull request or a GitHub issue. Describe the item; do not attach files of uncertain rights.

Please do not contact living participants unless a separately agreed research protocol exists. That work is out of scope for casual website contributions.
